key_concepts: The human body has five sense organs: eyes, ears, nose, tongue, and skin.
Eyes are used for seeing objects and can tell size, color, and shape.
Ears are used for hearing sounds and can tell whether sounds are loud or soft.
The nose is used for smelling and can tell good or bad odors.
The tongue is used for tasting and can identify sweet, sour, bitter, and salty flavors.
The skin is used for touching and feeling and can tell hot or cold.
Sense organs help people understand their surroundings.
Healthy habits protect the sense organs from diseases.
Keeping sense organs clean and eating a balanced diet help care for them.
Examples of eye care include not reading in dim light and wearing sunglasses on sunny days
Ears should be cleaned regularly but not pricked with objects.
Skin can be protected by bathing, cleaning hands, and avoiding direct sunlight.
